shortcut.title: Global shortcuts
shortcut.tip: Shortcuts apply to all terminals and can be sent in one tap from the terminal toolbar or the mobile key bar. With "Enter" off, the command is typed without being executed.
shortcut.name: Name

settings.title: Web Terminal settings
settings.allowLocalShellHelp: Required before connections of the "Local shell" type can be created and used
settings.localShellWarn: The local shell runs commands as the user running Gately, which amounts to full control of the server. Keep the admin interface off the public internet, use a strong password and enable two-factor authentication.
settings.maxSessionsHelp: Upper limit on terminal sessions, including those kept after a disconnect
settings.idleTimeoutHelp: A session with no input or output for this long is ended automatically. 0 means no limit.
settings.bufferSizeHelp: Size of recent output kept per session, used to restore the screen after a reconnect or page refresh
settings.heartbeatHelp: How often the browser and server exchange heartbeats, to keep the connection alive and detect drops early
settings.keepAliveHelp: How long a session keeps running after the browser disconnects, during which it can be re-attached. 0 ends the session on disconnect. Set a value above 0 to recover sessions after a page refresh.
settings.credentialsHelp: Save several passwords or private keys for SSH connections to pick from

agreementText:
Web Terminal User Agreement

1. Web Terminal lets you connect to SSH and Telnet servers directly from the browser, or start a local shell on the server running Gately, with SFTP file management. These capabilities amount to remote control of the target host. Use them only on devices you are authorized to manage.

2. The connection details you save (passwords, private keys, passphrases, etc.) are stored in Gately's configuration directory. Protect the configuration files and backups, set a strong password for the admin interface and enable two-factor authentication.

3. The local shell and SFTP file management run with the privileges of the user running Gately and can read and write every file that user can access. Do not expose the admin interface directly to the public internet.

4. You are solely responsible for all commands, file changes and deletions performed through Web Terminal. These operations are irreversible, so double-check before running high-risk commands.

5. By using this feature you confirm that you have read and agree to the above.
